codeReview.summary: The patch improves scheduled-status reporting, startup polling order, and quota-stop finalization, but two correctness gaps remain: overdue one-shot schedules still launch after their stop window has already passed, and conflicting live reschedules are rejected from the DB row only rather than the actual runtime state.

issues.description: launch_due_streams only skips expired windows for recurring schedules. For one-shot schedules, if the backend wakes up after both schedule_start_at and scheduled_stop_time are already in the past, the code still calls start_stream() and only relies on stop_due_streams later in the same poll to shut it back down. That can briefly publish a stream outside its requested window after scheduler downtime or delayed polling; the launcher should fail closed by skipping/clearing overdue one-shot schedules before any start attempt.

update_stream_schedule rejects conflicting scheduling based only on stream.status from the database row. If that field is stale while supervisor/systemd is still actively running the stream (for example before reconciliation after a backend restart or lease/status drift), PATCH /api/streams/{id} can persist a new future schedule onto a live stream, which violates the feature's requirement to reject conflicting live scheduling. This guard needs a runtime-aware check instead of trusting the stored status alone.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission/shared-state docs do not mention that DEV auth falls back to a built-in default identity when DEV_USER_EMAIL and DEV_USER_ID are absent, so workers have to reverse-engineer the effective local auth identity during API verification.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript for worker 6749ee33-6942-495e-b9bb-944dd68703e4 shows the worker grepping backend/.env, finding ENABLE_DEV_AUTH=true but no DEV_USER_EMAIL/DEV_USER_ID, then reading backend/app/api/deps.py. The fallback is implemented at backend/app/api/deps.py:190-195 (`email = settings.dev_user_email or "dev@example.com"`).

summary: Review failed. The feature landed useful scheduler/runtime fixes, but it still launches overdue one-shot schedules after their stop boundary has already passed and it still accepts future schedules based on a potentially stale DB status instead of the actual live runtime state. I also noted a shared-state gap around undocumented DEV-auth fallback defaults used for local verification.
